name: Effect set
purpose: House a family of single effects on one sheet: an overview rack, one technique block per effect (plate, dials, recipe, limits, live params), and a gallery of usages that run the same functions with the live dials.

files.sheet.css: styles on the T&T shell tokens
files.worker.js: render worker (same fx.js + set.js, off the main thread)

layout: head: set code, title, premise, how to use
material system: read, shared causes, pass order
sticky bar: loupe 4× · section jump links (#sec-<id>) · undo/redo · copy link · copy set params · reset all · status
rack: one header per section (number, title, blurb), one 4:3 cell per effect with kind · mechanism and mark count
sections: stocks → added → changed, each with a numbered heading and blurb

per effect: header (code · kind · mechanism, name, sub, prints on / stock for, reset · new seed) → presets → plate (sticky, 4:3, device px, light puck, stats: px · marks · ms · dpr) with views image · separation · stock · mask, distance, wedge, pin · split + dial column (tabs Mark · Field · Stock · Relief · Finish · Color · Edge, seed row) → output → recipe · lift · live spec
usages: masonry cards filtered by job, canvas + labels, caption, effect chips, overrides; toggle follow the dials | defaults only
contract: ground, color math, units, params, source, files, set.js shape

dials.tabs: Mark (motif + structure) · Field · Stock (transfer) · Relief · Finish · Color (color + film) · Edge; a tab that would hold one row folds into its neighbor under a small heading; the seed is a row under the tabs; a dot marks tabs and rows changed from default

groups.structure: geometry and counts of the marks or the stock
groups.field: how strength varies across the plate (value, pressure, dose, exposure, wear)
groups.transfer: how the mark meets the stock
groups.relief: heights in CSS px and how they shade
groups.finish: view-dependent terms (sheen, gloss, reflection, soft box, camera)
groups.film: how color combines (film thickness, color rule, overprint)
groups.seed: the single source of every random draw

dials.range: hairline track; limit zones hatched with the reason as title; default tick; tap the value to type it; double-click label resets
dials.light: puck in the bar: angle = azimuth, distance from center = elevation; arrow keys step it
dials.ink: swatch + oklch() + hex + "chroma reduced" flag; L/C/h tracks painted with the sweep
dials.mixing: five-row strip in the Color tab, only when the effect has a color rule (mix): white → ink in film · oklab · oklch · linear · srgb, current highlighted
dials.when: params that do not apply are dimmed, not hidden

rendering.workers: pool of up to 3 (hardwareConcurrency − 1) running worker.js; main-thread fallback on file://
rendering.draft: ½-res while dragging a dial or the light
rendering.scheduling: latest job per canvas wins; drafts first, then plates, usages, rack
rendering.lazy: IntersectionObserver (300 px margin); offscreen canvases go dirty and paint when they scroll in
rendering.coupling: a change to effect X redraws X, every effect whose stockOf() is X, and every usage that uses either
rendering.state: one params object per effect + the sheet light, saved per viewer in localStorage (try/catch)

sections.title: Stocks
sections.blurb: Paper and cloth as lit height fields. Every other effect reads their height, color and light.

sections.title: Added marks
sections.blurb: Something lands on the stock: ink, graphite, foil, varnish or thread. The stock's height decides where it takes.

sections.title: Changed in place
sections.blurb: The stock itself changes. A die presses it, sunlight turns a brushed coating blue, a laser burns it.

outputs.lin: Float32 W·H·3, lit linear RGB (diffuse light once, view-dependent light last)
outputs.alb: Float32 W·H·3, unlit albedo (what a later pass prints over)
outputs.lf: Float32 W·H·3, light factor from the sheet light
outputs.ink: Float32 W·H, this effect's own separation (plate), 0..1; the key stays ink, the UI and docs say separation
outputs.stock: Float32 W·H, height in CSS px: stock relief plus the effect's own relief
outputs.marks: count of marks; pixel counts are per CSS px², so they do not grow with dpr
